drug_interactions.reason: Ibuprofen can destabilize blood sugar levels when combined with Metformin, increasing the risk of hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia.
Aspirin may enhance the hypoglycemic effect of Metformin, requiring closer blood sugar monitoring.

NSAIDs like Ibuprofen can increase bleeding risk when combined with Warfarin.
NSAIDs can reduce the effectiveness of ACE inhibitors like Lisinopril and may cause kidney problems.
Amlodipine can increase simvastatin levels, raising the risk of muscle damage (rhabdomyolysis).
Ciprofloxacin can greatly increase tizanidine levels, causing severe low blood pressure and drowsiness.
Omeprazole may reduce the effectiveness of Clopidogrel, increasing cardiovascular risk.
Alcohol increases the risk of lactic acidosis when combined with Metformin.
High doses of Paracetamol may enhance the anticoagulant effect of Warfarin.

Calcium supplements can interfere with Levothyroxine absorption. Take 4 hours apart.
